rationale: The entry-kind read corrects the previous framing. Nodes 3 and 4 hold identical kinds at indices 35, 36 and 37: a decided value, the StopSign, and nothing. Their logs therefore agree at the reconfiguration position, and leader 4 did not lose the StopSign from its log. What differs is the cached state and the decided index: node 4 reports is_reconfigured None even though its log holds a StopSign at index 36, and it reports decided 38 while its accepted index is 37 and its log ends at index 36, so its decided index exceeds its own log. Node 3, which still has the StopSign in its cache, catches neither. This update records those facts, revises the question's hypothesis from a missing marker in the leader's log to a cleared cache plus a decided index beyond the local log, and restates the interpretation accordingly.

knowledge.statement: At the end of seeded run 13, nodes 3 and 4 both read index 35 as a decided value, index 36 as a StopSign and index 37 as absent. Node 3 reports is_reconfigured Some with accepted 37 and decided 37; node 4 reports is_reconfigured None with accepted 37 and decided 38. Node 4 therefore holds a StopSign entry at index 36 while its cached marker is absent, and its decided index of 38 exceeds its own accepted index of 37 and the last log position it holds.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; entry kinds are read once at the end at indices 35, 36 and 37, and is_reconfigured and the indices are sampled at the same point.

investigations.hypothesis: A follower holding a decided StopSign can be left behind when the current leader's decided index advances past its own log while the follower's accepted index ends at the StopSign. The leader reaches that decided index by counting follower-reported accepted indices in handle_accepted, without a matching local entry and without requiring decided <= accepted on itself. The Decides it sends are the follower's next expected sequence messages, so handle_decide clamps the follower's decided index to its accepted index instead of reconnecting, and no repair follows while that leader remains.

knowledge.assertion: Corrects the earlier framing: the two logs agree at indices 35 to 37, so the leader did not lose the StopSign entry. The observable split is the cached marker (None on the leader, Some on node 3) plus a leader decided index of 38 that exceeds its own accepted 37 and its last log position.
Still accurate about the sampled values, but its phrase 'leader 4 holds none' refers to the cached marker; the entry-kind read shows the leader's log does hold a StopSign at index 36.

This is the mechanism that produced decided 38 on a node whose accepted index is 37: handle_accepted counts follower-reported accepted indices and sets the decided index without comparing it to the leader's own accepted index.
Explains how the leader's cached StopSign can be absent while its log entry remains: sync_log clears only the cached marker, not the previously appended StopSign entry.

interpretations.rationale: The executed receipts locate the stall in the leader's decided index and cached marker rather than in a missing StopSign entry. Receipt 52257864a0274ef08c8a738fdd9420de ran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed); its comparison (converged_all true, gated on progressed and reconfigured) is complete and violated on event 1, which reports decided 38,38,37,38,38 after 150 fair-delivery rounds. That event records, for both node 3 and node 4, index 35 as a decided value, index 36 as a StopSign and index 37 as absent, so the two logs agree at the reconfiguration position and leader 4 did not lose the StopSign entry. What differs is the other state: node 3 reports is_reconfigured Some with accepted 37 and decided 37, while node 4 reports is_reconfigured None with accepted 37 and decided 38. Leader 4 thus has a StopSign in its log at 36 but no cached marker, which is exactly what sync_log's clearing branch leaves behind when a later LogSync with stopsign None is applied: the cached field is cleared while the appended entry is not removed. Its decided index of 38 also exceeds its own accepted index of 37 and the last position it holds, which handle_accepted permits because it sets the decided index from a follower-reported accepted index once is_chosen counts a quorum, without comparing that index to the leader's own accepted index. Node 3, still holding the cached StopSign, receives the Decides with sequence counters 2 and 3 as its next expected messages; handle_decide clamps decided to its accepted 37 and never reconnects, as its trace prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|prepare:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|promise:0-0>0-0|accsync1:0-0>37-0|decide2:37-0>37-37|decide3:37-37>37-37 shows. The periodic resend path offers no AcceptStopSign because node 3 already accepted one, and repeated Decides reuse a consumed sequence number, so nothing repairs the follower while leader 4 remains. The zero divergence count is not evidence of agreement: the harness keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix, so StopSign entries and prefix lengths are never compared. The two nodes do agree on the kinds they hold, but the leader's decided index of 38 refers to a position that neither node's log contains.
counterevidence: A follower that genuinely missed the AcceptStopSign can still recover: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead, the follower reconnected, and an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, which gives the follower a fresh sequence and a log sync from the new leader.
The two logs agree at indices 35 to 37, so this is not a value or marker divergence between node 3 and leader 4 at those positions.
Leader 4's cached marker being absent while its log holds a StopSign shows the cached field and the log can disagree, so is_reconfigured alone is not a reliable indicator of the log contents.
limitations: Entry kinds and is_reconfigured are sampled once at the end, so the receipt does not show when the cached marker was cleared or when the decided index passed the local log.
Node 3's inbound trace is capped at twelve messages after the lossy phase, and Promises to node 4 are recorded only when delivered and only up to forty entries.
The divergence check keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix, so it cannot detect a StopSign-versus-value disagreement or a length difference.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
